title: Bounded D1 relationship batch reads
problem: Primary created-at reports can now resolve complete cohorts larger than one hundred relationships while concrete D1 persistence readers still construct one relationship-id IN clause for the entire logical cohort.
semantics: Each persistence owner retains its existing canonical relationship-id validation and deduplication.
Cohorts larger than one hundred are split into deterministic contiguous chunks of at most one hundred relationship IDs.
Each bounded chunk re-enters the existing concrete persistence read contract so existing SQL, hydration, validation, and failure behavior remain authoritative.
Any failed chunk fails the full logical persistence read.
Empty cohorts continue to perform zero SELECTs.
Merged results are restored to the existing global relationship-id ordering.
Rows belonging to the same relationship never cross chunks after canonical deduplication, so their existing per-query SQL ordering remains intact.
Presentation retains its existing four-query-family behavior for chunks containing insurance profiles.
Economics retains separate acquisition-cost, premium, commission, and renewal persistence methods.
Outcomes retain the existing relationship_id ASC, occurred_at ASC, outcome_fact_id ASC ordering contract.
tests: Shared chunk helper proves 100 plus 1 deterministic partitioning.
Presentation proves a 101-relationship cohort binds as 100 plus 1 and preserves global relationship ordering.
Every economics batch method proves a 101-relationship cohort executes exactly two bounded SELECTs.
Acquisition-cost batching additionally proves global relationship ordering across chunk boundaries.
Outcome batching proves exactly two bounded SELECTs and global relationship ordering across chunk boundaries.
